model: Atari Video Computer System (CX2600, six-switch, Taiwan-made)

sources.quote: Atari 2600 videogames console, Atari, designed USA, 1977; manufactured Taiwan, 1978-1982
six metal cylindrical switches on top, with a slot for a videogame cartridge.
Insert the Game Program CAREFULLY into the slot in the center of the Console unit switch panel.

notes: Envelope: Victoria and Albert Museum B.15-2022 (O1509988), 'Atari 2600', object type 'Videogames console', measured 17/12/2021 with the part named 'main console' (the record also holds joysticks, controllers, a cartridge and packaging, measured separately or not at all). V&A labels each axis: height 89 mm, width 346 mm, depth 232 mm, filed as printed. Whether projections (switch levers) are included is not stated: excludes_projections null. No mass is published.

Why this is the light sixer: the record describes 'six metal cylindrical switches on top' and dates the unit 'manufactured Taiwan, 1978-1982', and its production note says 'Initially manufactured in Sunnyvale, California, from September 1977, production was moved to Taiwan in 1978'. A six-switch Taiwan-made CX2600 is the shell collectors call the light sixer; the V&A does not use that name, and the key is our reading of the record. atari-2600-cx2600 (the 1977 Sunnyvale heavy sixer) keeps body null.

controls and media also cite Atari's 1977 'Model CX2600' owner's manual (archive.org scan, OCR text layer, primary), which covers the six-switch CX2600 without separating the two shells; see atari-2600-cx2600 for the reading of its panel caption (all seven switches filed as slide_switch, the contract's VCS-panel kind). ports not filed (no connector types named).
external_ids are the platform's: Wikidata Q206261 'Atari 2600' (API), igdb_platform from its P5795.
